````text
# #4632: Patch: follow-up to #4625 from the after-merge spot-check
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

<!-- jackioh-bot:spot-check-follow-up #4625 -->
The after-merge spot-check of #4625 ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/45262298713)) found 1 blocking problem(s) in the change as it merged (`d6a44a6e7891`). `claude-6` (claude, `opus`, strong) reviewed it. #4625 stays merged: nothing is reverted, and this issue fixes what it found in a change of its own, from `main`.

## What to fix

- [ ] `apps/web/src/audio/music-ui.test.tsx:163`: No test fails if musicScene.ts's leave() goes back to a synchronous apply(), so the PR's riskiest piece, the deferred hand-back behind the 'no menu theme between two boards' rule (R4606000, issue acceptance item 2), is unproven.
  Evidence: With nothing holding the menu theme, musicScene.ts apply() requests `{ track: null }`, not the menu track (`menuHolders > 0 ? { track: MENU_TRACK, … } : { track: null }`). The new tests 'R4606000 two boards of one match in a single commit never ask for the menu theme' (music-ui.test.tsx:163), ReplayPlayer.test.tsx:781, DuosBoard.test.tsx:545 and DuosReplay.test.tsx:461 never call holdMenuMusic() (grep finds it only at music-ui.test.tsx:121 and :177), and their beforeEach hooks do not either. So a synchronous hand-back between unmount and remount would request `{track: null}`, and `.some(r => r.track === "menu")` would still be false. The `wanted` checks read only the last request, which is the new board's game track either way. Fix: in those tests, push `holdMenuMusic()` (released in afterEach as music-ui does) before mounting, and also assert that no request after the first game request has `track === null`. Then reverting `scheduleApply()` to `apply()` turns them red.

## Done when

- Each finding above is fixed where it points, or answered with the evidence that it does not hold.
- Every check is green, with no test skipped, ignored or weakened to get there (CLAUDE.md rule 12).

---
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot from the after-merge spot-check (one in 5 medium or hard merges, `spot_check_every`): `muse` (`muse`) built #4625 and `muse` (`muse-spark-1.3-contributor`) approved it. This issue's own pull request is never spot-checked.

<!-- jackioh-bot -->

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `claude-3` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/45266800033)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

The finding says no test fails if `leave()` in `apps/web/src/audio/musicScene.ts` hands the music back synchronously. **That claim does not hold, and the plan answers it with evidence.** I also checked the suggested fix, and it would break a test that passes today.

- **Why the finding is wrong.** A mounted `Game` holds the menu theme itself. `useGameAudio.ts:132` calls `retainAppAudio()`, and `appAudio.ts:26` calls `holdMenuMusic()`. So while a board is leaving, `menuHolders > 0`, and a synchronous `apply()` requests `{ track: "menu" }`, not `{ track: null }`.
- **Mutation run.** I made `scheduleApply()`'s microtask run synchronously, which is the same as reverting it to `apply()`. All four existing R4606000 tests went red on their "no menu theme" assertions:
  - `music-ui.test.tsx`, "two boards of one match in a single commit…"
  - `ReplayPlayer.test.tsx:782`
  - `DuosBoard.test.tsx:545`
  - `DuosReplay.test.tsx:461`
- **Why the suggested fix is wrong for `music-ui`.** `releases.push(holdMenuMusic())` before mounting makes that test fail on the current code. The test unmounts and renders in two separate `act` calls. In between, the board's own last-holder release (`releaseMenu()`) calls `apply()` synchronously. In the app, `main.tsx:979` holds `retainAppAudio()` for the page's whole life, so that release never happens. The tests have no such hold. The suggested `track === null` assertion fails on the current code for the same reason.
- **What to deliver.** Leave the four board tests alone. Add `apps/web/src/audio/musicScene.test.ts`, which pins the deferred hand-back on `musicScene.ts` alone, with no board and no incidental hold. It goes red when `leave()` calls `apply()` directly. Then report the mutation evidence in the final report.

## Files to touch

| Path | New/change | What |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/audio/musicScene.test.ts` | new | Three `it("R4606000 …")` tests on `enterGameMusic`, `holdMenuMusic` and `gameMusicClaims`, with a recording `MusicPlayer`. |
| `spec/rulings/R4606000.md` | change | Add `  - apps/web/src/audio/musicScene.test.ts` to the end of `proven_in`. Change nothing else in the note. |

Must not touch:
- `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`.
- `apps/web/src/audio/musicScene.ts`. The mutation check edits it temporarily and must restore it.
- The four board test files.
- `spec/11-rulings.md`, `spec/INDEX.md`, `spec/CARDS.md`, and `spec/pending/4606.md`.
- Any Rust crate.

Governing spec: §10.11 "Music" and R631, as amended by R4606000. No new ruling is made, so no new note or `spec/pending` entry is needed.

## Steps

1. **Create `apps/web/src/audio/musicScene.test.ts`.**

   Header comment, three lines, citing R4606000. It says: a board leaving hands the music back on a microtask. The board tests prove it through a mounted `Game`, which holds the menu theme itself (`useGameAudio` → `retainAppAudio`), so a synchronous hand-back asks for `{ track: "menu" }` there. This file proves it on `musicScene.ts` alone.

   Imports:
   - `afterEach`, `describe`, `expect`, `it` from `vitest`
   - `setMusicPlayerForTests`, `type MusicPlayer`, `type MusicRequest` from `./music.ts`
   - `MENU_TRACK` from `./musicData.ts` (its value is `"menu"`)
   - `enterGameMusic`, `gameMusicClaims`, `holdMenuMusic` from `./musicScene.ts`

   Add the following:
   - **`recordingPlayer()`.** Copy it verbatim from `apps/web/src/replay/ReplayPlayer.test.tsx` lines 36–58. It returns `MusicPlayer & { requests: MusicRequest[] }`.
   - **Constants:**
     - `GAME: MusicRequest = { track: "tavern-1", opponentTurn: false }`
     - `MENU: MusicRequest = { track: MENU_TRACK, opponentTurn: false }`
     - `SILENCE: MusicRequest = { track: null }`
   - **`async function flushMicrotasks(): Promise<void> { await Promise.resolve(); }`.** The queued callback goes first in the FIFO queue, so it runs before the continuation.
   - **A shared `let player`.** Each test makes it with `player = recordingPlayer(); setMusicPlayerForTests(player);` as its first lines.
   - **`afterEach`.** `setMusicPlayerForTests(null);`. Every test must leave `gameMusicClaims()` at 0 and release its holds, because the module state is global to the file.

2. **Add test 1 (the leave itself asks for nothing).**
   - Title: `R4606000 a board leaving asks for nothing in the leave itself and hands the menu theme back on a microtask`.
   - Body:
     ```ts
     const release = holdMenuMusic();
     const board = enterGameMusic();
     board.request(GAME);
     const before = player.requests.length;
     board.leave();
     expect(player.requests.length, "the leave itself asks for nothing").toBe(before);
     await flushMicrotasks();
     expect(player.requests.slice(before)).toEqual([MENU]);
     expect(gameMusicClaims()).toBe(0);
     release();
     ```
   - Under a synchronous `apply()` this fails on the first `expect`.

3. **Add test 2 (a board entering first claims the music).**
   - Title: `R4606000 a board entering before the microtask claims the music with no menu theme or silence between`.
   - Body:
     ```ts
     const release = holdMenuMusic();
     const first = enterGameMusic();
     first.request(GAME);
     const before = player.requests.length;
     first.leave();
     const second = enterGameMusic();
     second.request(GAME);
     await flushMicrotasks();
     const asked = player.requests.slice(before);
     expect(asked.some((r) => r.track === MENU_TRACK)).toBe(false);
     expect(asked.some((r) => r.track === null)).toBe(false);
     expect(asked.at(-1)).toEqual(GAME);
     second.leave();
     await flushMicrotasks();
     release();
     ```
   - Under a synchronous `apply()` the menu request appears and this fails.

4. **Add test 3 (a real exit with nothing holding the menu theme).**
   - Title: `R4606000 a board leaving with nothing holding the menu theme asks for silence on the microtask`.
   - Body:
     ```ts
     const board = enterGameMusic();
     board.request(GAME);
     const before = player.requests.length;
     board.leave();
     expect(player.requests.length).toBe(before);
     await flushMicrotasks();
     expect(player.requests.slice(before)).toEqual([SILENCE]);
     ```
   - This pins the `{ track: null }` branch that the finding's evidence mentions.

5. **Edit `spec/rulings/R4606000.md`.** In the front matter, after `  - apps/web/src/duos/DuosReplay.test.tsx`, add a line `  - apps/web/src/audio/musicScene.test.ts`.

6. **Run the mutation check and keep the output for the report.**
   1. In `apps/web/src/audio/musicScene.ts`, change the line inside `leave()` (line 96) from `scheduleApply();` to `apply();`.
   2. Run the five files (command under Tests). Expect red in all five: the four board tests on their menu assertions, and `musicScene.test.ts` tests 1–3.
   3. Edit the line back to `scheduleApply();`. Confirm `git diff --stat -- apps/web/src/audio/musicScene.ts` prints nothing. Do not use `git reset`, `stash` or `checkout`.
   4. Re-run the five files and expect green.

7. **Write the final report.** Include the commands you ran and the mutation run's red and green lines. State that the finding's claim (no test fails on a synchronous hand-back) does not hold for the four board tests, with the reason from **Goal**. State that its suggested fix was not applied because it turns `music-ui`'s test red on current code. Name the decisions below.

**Decisions made, with the rejected alternative:**
- Left the four board tests unchanged. The alternative was to add `holdMenuMusic()` and a `track === null` assertion as the issue suggests. That breaks `music-ui`, and the other three already go red under the mutation.
- Proved the rule in a new unit test on `musicScene.ts`. The alternative was a page-level `retainAppAudio()` in each board test, which touches four files for no extra proof.
- Used `holdMenuMusic()` in the unit test, not `retainAppAudio()`. There is no board in that test to cause the release path.

## Tests

**New file:** `apps/web/src/audio/musicScene.test.ts`, with the three tests above.

**Commands.** Build the WASM once (it is git-ignored), then run from the repository root:

```
sh scripts/build-wasm.sh
pnpm exec vitest run --project web apps/web/src/audio/musicScene.test.ts apps/web/src/audio/music-ui.test.tsx apps/web/src/replay/ReplayPlayer.test.tsx apps/web/src/duos/DuosBoard.test.tsx apps/web/src/duos/DuosReplay.test.tsx
pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck
pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/audio/musicScene.test.ts
cargo jackioh spec check
```

The harness's own web-test step excludes `**/src/audio/**`, so run these files yourself.

## Done when

- [ ] `musicScene.test.ts` exists with the three tests, all green on unmodified `musicScene.ts`.
- [ ] The mutation run (`scheduleApply()` → `apply()` in `leave()`) turns the new tests and the four board tests red. `musicScene.ts` is restored: `git diff` on it is empty.
- [ ] `spec/rulings/R4606000.md` lists the new file in `proven_in`, and `cargo jackioh spec check` passes.
- [ ] The four board test files and `musicScene.ts` are unchanged.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check`, the web typecheck and eslint on the new file pass. No test is skipped, ignored or weakened, and no `eslint-disable` or `@ts-*` is added.
- [ ] The report states that the finding's premise is false, with the mutation evidence, and says why its suggested fix was not applied.

## Risks

- **Module state.** `musicScene.ts` keeps `menuHolders`, `claims` and `applyQueued` as module globals. Every test must release its holds, leave its boards and flush microtasks, or a later test sees a stale hold. Vitest isolates modules per file, so nothing leaks across files.
- **Forgotten mutation.** A forgotten `apply()` edit would ship a behaviour regression. Step 6 requires restoring the line and checking the diff.
- **Spec check.** The `proven_in` path must hold an `it(` title with `R4606000` as a word and no `.skip`, `.only` or `.todo`. The three titles above all start with it.
- **Reviewer expectations.** The harness reviewer may expect the suggested fix. The report's evidence is the answer, and the issue's "Done when" allows answering a finding with evidence that it does not hold.
- **Purity and hidden information.** No Rust crate, engine rule or hidden information is touched, so CLAUDE.md rules 4 and 7 are unaffected.

## Open questions

None.
````
